fixes.explanation: Eight it is. Josiah, king of Judah, takes the throne at eight and reigns in Jerusalem thirty-one years. I can't stick with a gym membership for thirty-one days. This boy stuck with a kingdom.

Twelve is in this story, but it's a different number. The twelfth year of his reign is when Josiah begins cleansing Judah and Jerusalem. Josiah, king of Judah, was eight when he became king, so you grabbed a real number from the story and hung it on a different peg. Happens to me with oven timers all the time.

That's the one. Josiah did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the ways of his father David. The text adds that he did not turn aside to the right or to the left. A straight line, friend, and I can't even cut one through a cookie sheet.

Not this king. The text says Josiah did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. He walked in the ways of his father David and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. I can see why a kid king might sound risky, but this one is a good surprise.

True. In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, Josiah began to seek the God of his father David. Josiah, king of Judah, was young, and he began seeking God. That's a good place to start, friend.

It's actually true. The text says that in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, Josiah began to seek the God of his father David. Josiah was king of Judah. Easy one to second-guess when you're looking for a trap, friend.

Right on target. In his twelfth year Josiah began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved idols, and the cast images. That's a long list, and he works through it. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer and never cleared out a single thing.

No merchants on this list. What the text says Josiah cleared out is the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved idols, and the cast images. He began that cleansing in his twelfth year. Merchants and traders just aren't named there, friend.
The text says the opposite. The altars of the Baals were torn down in his presence. Josiah, king of Judah, was right there for it. Hands-on kings are rare, and this one is one.
False is right. The text says the altars of the Baals were torn down in his presence. Josiah, king of Judah, was there when it happened. So staying back at the palace doesn't fit what the verse says.
Back to Jerusalem it is. After tearing down the altars and Asherah poles throughout the land of Israel, the text says he returned to Jerusalem. That's the city where he reigned.

Hebron never comes up in this passage. The text says Josiah returned to Jerusalem after tearing down the altars and Asherah poles throughout the land of Israel. Josiah was king of Judah, and Jerusalem was where he reigned. Easy to pick another city name when you're guessing, but this verse names the one.

Task by task is the answer. The text says the Levites over the laborers supervised all who did the work, task by task. That's steady attention, not a drive-by. It's like checking each tray as it goes in, and I only learned that after a few sad batches.

That's right. The text says some of the Levites were secretaries, officers, and gatekeepers. They're the ones who kept the records and the doors in order. Some of the Levites held jobs like these, and the text names them.
